title: Strategies to increase uptake of bereavement follow-up offered by a palliative care service: a rapid review
subtitle: Rapid review to inform the redesign of a hospice bereavement programme
statement: The hospice offers bereavement follow-up to every family after a death, but in 2025 only 71 of 412 eligible families took up any support, and uptake was lowest among men, families who needed an interpreter and families living far from the hospice. The board has asked for a redesigned programme by December 2026. A rapid review will summarise what is known about strategies that increase uptake of bereavement follow-up offered by palliative care services, so that the redesign rests on evidence rather than opinion.
whoAffected: Bereaved family members of patients who die in the hospice or under the community team, especially men, families who need an interpreter and families living more than an hour away; the volunteers and social worker who deliver follow-up; and the board that decides the redesign.
whatHurts: Most families receive a card and at most one call, and few take up support. Families who might benefit most may never hear an offer they can accept, while the small team's time goes to routine calls that many families decline.
currentPractice: Condolence card at two weeks; volunteer phone call at six weeks offering a monthly support group or one-to-one support with the social worker; no risk screening; no interpreter-supported or text-based offer.
whyNow: The board requires a redesign proposal on 9 December 2026, colleagues disagree about timing, text messages and risk screening, and the hospice director has approved librarian and reviewer time for a short evidence review.
constraints: Eight weeks until the board meeting on 9 December 2026. No funding for the review; the hospice librarian for two working days and the social worker as second reviewer for about 20 percent of screening. English-language sources only.
patientCenteredGoal: Every bereaved family receives a clear, timely offer of support in a form they can take up, and families at higher risk of prolonged grief are not missed.
summary: Problem framed as a rapid review of strategies that increase uptake of bereavement follow-up, to inform a board decision in December 2026.
